{{Quote|And let me remind you of our absolute commitment to capitalism&hellip; to the lower taxes, the reduced tariffs, and the eventual abolition of all trade barriers. Signing this treaty will bring you profits beyond your wildest imagination. What we are proposing is complete free trade.|Count Dooku, to major galactic business leaders|<ref name="AOTC novel">[[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'' novelization]]</ref>}}
[[File:SecessionistMovement.png|thumb|right|300px|Count Dooku promised the Separatist Council that the Separatist Alliance was dedicated to capitalism and would usher in a new era of profit.]]
'''Capitalism''' was an economic and political system used in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="AOTC novel" /> In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> during a business meeting<ref name="Umbara Commentary">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Four|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' The Complete Season Four]], "Darkened World of Umbara" Commentary</ref> with major [[Galaxy|galactic]] business leaders who sat on the [[Separatist Council/Legends|Separatist Council]], [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] promised the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] (CIS) was totally faithful to capitalism, promising that their support would increase their profits to unseen levels thanks to completely free trade: Dooku stated the CIS would offer lower taxes and reduced tariffs, with the ultimate aim of removing all barriers to trade.<ref name="AOTC novel" /> Ultimately, the corporations agreed to help Dooku and his confederacy. However, such companies were also were willing to maintain business with the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] to profit off both factions in the ensuing [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="Umbara Commentary" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|And let me remind you of our absolute commitment to capitalism&hellip; of the lower taxes, the reduced tariffs, and the eventual abolition of all trade barriers. Signing this treaty will bring you profits beyond your wildest imagination.|Count Dooku, in the ''Attack of the Clones'' script|<ref name="EpIIScript">{{WebCite|url=https://assets.scriptslug.com/live/pdf/scripts/star-wars-episode-ii-attack-of-the-clones-2002.pdf|text=''Star Wars'' Episode II ''Attack of the Clones''|author=[[George Lucas]], [[Jonathan Hales]]|archivedate=20250324014207}}</ref>}}
[[Wikipedia:Capitalism|Capitalism]] is a real-world economic model that was first mentioned within the ''[[Star Wars]]'' universe through the script of<ref name="StarWarsFordham">{{WebCite|url=https://fordhampoliticalreview.org/star-wars-america-from-a-certain-point-of-view|text=Star Wars: America from a Certain Point of View|author=Capucine Fourleignie Baufumé |date=2023-11-06|archivedate=20250117045310}}</ref> the [[2002]]<ref name="AttackClones">{{Film|II}}</ref> film [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']].<ref name="StarWarsFordham" /> In the [[July 4]], [[2000]]&ndash;dated script by [[George Lucas]] and [[Jonathan Hales]], Dooku mentions to the corporate leaders<ref name="EpIIScript" /> who will become the Separatist Council<ref name="AttackClones" /> that his Separatist state will have an "absolute commitment to capitalism," which will entail reduced taxes and tariffs, which will, in time, be followed by the abolition of any barrier to trade. Concluding his pitch to these leaders to sign onto the CIS, he promises the government will allow their profits to reach unseen levels.<ref name="EpIIScript" />

While Dooku's line is cut down in the final film,<ref name="AttackClones" /> removing the outright mention of capitalism,<ref name="StarWarsFordham" /> its mention was retained in the [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|novelization]] by [[R. A. Salvatore]],<ref name="AOTC novel" /> the [[Attack of the Clones (Mighty Chronicles)|Mighty Chronicles adaptation]] by [[John Whitman]],<ref name="Mighty Chronicles">[[Attack of the Clones (Mighty Chronicles)|''Attack of the Clones'' Mighty Chronicles adaptation]]</ref> and [[Star Wars: Episode II — Attack of the Clones 3|issue three]] of its [[Star Wars: Episode II — Attack of the Clones (comic series)|comic book adaption]] by [[Henry Gilroy]].<ref name="ATOC3">[[Star Wars: Episode II — Attack of the Clones 3|''Star Wars: Episode II — Attack of the Clones'' 3]]</ref> Therefore, capitalism was first outright mentioned in a ''Star Wars'' source through the novelization<ref name="AOTC novel" /> and Mighty Chronicles adaptation,<ref name="Mighty Chronicles" /> which were both released on [[April 23]], [[2002]],<ref name="YearByYear">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]''</ref><ref name="DateMighty">{{SWArchive|url=episode-ii/release/publish/news20020211.html|text=Book Preview: Mighty Chronicles}}</ref> ahead of the film itself on [[May 16]] of that year.<ref name="YearByYear" /> Meanwhile, ''Attack of the Clones'' issue three had been released on [[May 1]] of that year.<ref name="Dark Horse">{{DarkHorse|url=Comics/00-474/Star-Wars-Episode-II----Attack-of-the-Clones-3|text=Star Wars: Episode II -- Attack of the Clones #3}}</ref>

[[File:InvisibleHandROTS.png|thumb|left|300px|The Separatist command ship ''Invisible Hand'' shares its name with the "invisible hand" theory of capitalist economics.]]
Elsewhere in the [[prequel trilogy]], in the opening to the [[2005]] prequel film [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']],<ref name="RevengeSith">{{Film|III}}</ref> Separatist [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] is shown to be in command of a [[Starship/Legends|starship]] known as the ''[[Invisible Hand/Legends|Invisible Hand]]''. In the real world, one theory surrounding capitalism is economist [[Wikipedia:Adam Smith|Adam Smith's]] idea of the "[[Wikipedia:Invisible hand|invisible hand]]" of the market.<ref name="StarWarsFordham" /> The ''Invisible Hand'' name was coined by [[Matthew Stover]], author of the [[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]], "as a sort of inside joke," as he revealed in [[2025]]; according to Stover, the name functions as both a way to allude to Palpatine as the secret puppet master behind the Clone Wars and "a subtle dig at the conservatives who idolize Adam Smith." Stover made the latter point because of the connection between the Trade Federation and the robber barons of real-world history.<ref name="RotsDeluxe">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]], [[2025]] Deluxe Edition</ref>
